analysis.investment_thesis: CPPLUS trades at INR 2,264 — approximately 7.5x my calculated Graham Number of ~INR 301 (based on EPS ~₹29.8 and BVPS ~₹134.7), offering zero margin of safety. The 2025 net profit surge to ₹351 Cr is almost entirely illusory, driven by ₹259 Cr in "Other Income" against operating cash flow of a mere ₹27 Cr.
key_strengths: Debt/Equity of 0.08 — an unusually clean balance sheet, borrowings reduced to ₹128 Cr in FY25
Five consecutive years of positive reported earnings (2020–2025) — passes the basic continuity test
Revenue CAGR of 20.2% over five years showing real business growth in a growing surveillance market
key_risks: Valuation is absurd: P/E of 105x and P/B of 16x against my hard limits of 15x and 1.5x respectively
Earnings quality is severely impaired: ₹351 Cr net profit in FY25 rests on ₹259 Cr Other Income, while operating cash flow is only ₹27 Cr — the business earned almost nothing in cash
Free cash flow was -₹187 Cr in FY24 and essentially zero (₹1 Cr) in FY25 — reported profits are not translating to real cash
red_flags: Graham Number ~₹301 vs. market price of ₹2,264 — an 87% premium to intrinsic value by my formula
FY25 Other Income of ₹259 Cr nearly equals total operating income of ₹248 Cr — operating business alone earns almost nothing extra
OCF turned sharply negative in FY24 (-₹180 Cr) and barely recovered in FY25 (₹27 Cr) despite a tripling of reported net profit — working capital destruction is a serious concern
No disclosed dividend — shareholders receive no cash return from the business
analysis.detailed_analysis:
By every quantitative standard I have applied for fifty years, CPPLUS is a speculation masquerading as an investment. A P/E of 105x demands that the company sustain extraordinary growth for a decade without interruption — a condition I have never found reliable enough to pay for. A P/B of 16x means the investor is paying ₹16 for every ₹1 of net assets; at that price, even a modest contraction in margins or a sector slowdown destroys the entire equity cushion. The Graham Number of approximately ₹301 — derived from ₹29.8 EPS and ₹134.7 book value per share — tells me in plain arithmetic that the current price embeds no margin of safety whatsoever.

The earnings quality problem is equally troubling. FY2025 net profit more than tripled to ₹351 Cr, yet operating cash flow was only ₹27 Cr. The gap is explained almost entirely by ₹259 Cr of "Other Income" — a line I treat with the deepest suspicion when it exceeds the operating profit of the core business. In FY2024, the company burned ₹187 Cr in free cash flow. A business that cannot convert its stated profits into cash is not, in my judgment, earning those profits at all. Mr. Market has priced this company for perfection; the disciplined investor must demand a discount, not a premium.
